title: JSON mode field-level fallback and repair harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build an automated test harness that exercises field-level fallback and repair behaviors for JSON mode structured outputs. The harness will validate behavior when individual fields violate schema constraints in streaming, interleaved tool-calling, and partial-emission scenarios. We want deterministic coverage of common failure modes, measurable recovery rates, and latency/cost trade-offs so runtime policies (fallback -> retry -> repair -> escalate) can be tuned.
background: We already have broad schema/gating tests and constrained-decoder fuzz suites. However, current suites treat schema violations as monolithic failures. Product asks for more granular behaviour: allow safe, auditable field-level repairs when a single field deviates (e.g., type mismatch or missing required field) instead of failing the entire response. This ticket focuses on a harness that simulates problematic model outputs, evaluates repair strategies, and surfaces metrics for policy decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can inject deterministic field-level violations across 1k synthetic prompt templates and produce a reproducible dataset of failures

Define and exercise three repair strategies: in-place rewrite (constraint-guided rewrite), tool-assisted repair (invoke validation tool/function), and conservative fallback (return partial with sentinel and error metadata)
Measure repair success rate, end-to-end latency delta, and token-cost delta per strategy and publish a comparative table
Verify streaming partial-emission recovery: when a field is emitted late or fragmented across stream chunks, harness must simulate and validate recovery logic without duplicating fields
Must cover interleaved toolcall scenarios where the model emits a tool call, tool returns a value that violates schema, and the runtime triggers repair policies
Expose test outputs as CSV and JSON artifacts that can be consumed by Console QA dashboards

No regression on existing strict-mode testbeds: run harness against runtime-canary and ensure failing rate decrease <= 10% for P0 guardrails (i.e., harness must not weaken strict enforcement unintentionally)
test_plan: Create grammar-guided mutation engine that produces field-level violations: type flips, truncated arrays, swapped keys, extra unknown keys, and controlled token insertions
Generate 1k prompt templates across verticals (chat, completion, toolcall, embed+metadata) with seeds for deterministic runs
Run three repair strategies for each failure seed and record metrics: success boolean, repair attempts, tokens emitted, elapsed ms, and schema delta
Simulate streaming with variable chunk boundaries (1-8 tokens per chunk) to exercise partial emission handling and reassembly logic
Simulate KV-cache replay scenarios by injecting suffix/prefix mismatches and verifying cache-aware repairs do not corrupt KV offsets
Simulate toolcall interference: harness mocks tool return values that intentionally violate schema to test runtime reconciliation
Automate canary runs against runtime-1.21 (canary cluster) and compare against baseline run produced by current strict-decoder testbed
Publish a dashboard: pass/fail rates, top failing prompt templates, per-strategy latency/cost tradeoffs, and recommended default policy
Create a follow-up PR template listing runtime changes required for enabling field-level repair in non-P0 paths
